steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable component creation and state management for our legacy code simulation.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks for a component
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building a React component with state management capabilities.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for creating components and managing state in our legacy code simulation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the LegacyCodeSimulator component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named LegacyCodeSimulator that returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name LegacyCodeSimulator that returns a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the LegacyCodeSimulator component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named LegacyCodeSimulator is defined, returning an empty div element.
successCriteria: The component is named LegacyCodeSimulator and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the LegacyCodeSimulator component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but ensure it's named exactly LegacyCodeSimulator and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is not properly defined. Create a function named LegacyCodeSimulator that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize state for legacy system status
steps.instruction: Inside your LegacyCodeSimulator component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'status' and initialize it with the string value 'operational'.
steps.hint: Remember to call useState with the initial value, and destructure the returned array into the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for system health
const [health, setHealth] = useState('healthy');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a state variable 'status' that tracks the current status of the legacy system, starting as 'operational'.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with 'operational' as the initial value, and the returned array is destructured into a variable named 'status' and its setter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track the legacy system's status. This is a foundational step for managing system state during rewrites.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useState correctly. Make sure you're destructuring the array into 'status' and its setter, and initializing it with 'operational'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to call useState('operational') inside the component and destructure the result into [status, setStatus].

steps.title: Initialize state for technical debt level
steps.instruction: Inside the LegacyCodeSimulator component, use useState to create a state variable named 'technicalDebt' initialized to 75.
steps.hint: Add a second useState call after your existing state. The syntax is: const [technicalDebt, setTechnicalDebt] = useState(75);
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for technical debt
const [technicalDebt, setTechnicalDebt] = useState(75);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two state variables: one for legacy system status and one for technical debt level.
successCriteria: A 'technicalDebt' state variable is declared with useState and initialized to 75.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track the technical debt level in the legacy system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named 'technicalDebt' initialized to 75.
steps.feedbackWrong: The technical debt state wasn't properly initialized. Check that you're using useState with the correct variable name and initial value.

steps.title: Initialize state for rewrite progress
steps.instruction: Inside the LegacyCodeSimulator component, use useState to create a state variable named 'rewriteProgress' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after your existing state declarations. The syntax is: const [rewriteProgress, setRewriteProgress] = useState(0);
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a progress tracking state
const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'rewriteProgress' state variable is added to track the progress percentage of the rewrite project.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that creates 'rewriteProgress' state initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track rewrite progress. This is essential for monitoring the migration from legacy systems.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a state variable named 'rewriteProgress' and initialized it to 0 using useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rewrite progress state hasn't been properly initialized. Remember to use useState with an initial value of 0.

steps.title: Create handler for accumulating technical debt
steps.instruction: Inside the LegacyCodeSimulator component, create a function named accumulateDebt that increases the technicalDebt state by 5 when called.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses the setTechnicalDebt updater function to increment the current technicalDebt value by 5.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named accumulateDebt is defined inside the component that increases technicalDebt by 5.
successCriteria: The accumulateDebt function is defined and uses setTechnicalDebt to increase technicalDebt by 5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a function that simulates accumulating technical debt in the legacy system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly increments the technicalDebt state by 5 using setTechnicalDebt.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't properly increase the technicalDebt state. Try creating a function named accumulateDebt that uses setTechnicalDebt to add 5 to the current technicalDebt value.

steps.title: Create handler for starting rewrite project
steps.instruction: Create a function named startRewrite that sets legacyStatus to 'rewrite-in-progress' and resets technicalDebt to 0.
steps.hint: Define a function inside your component that calls setLegacyStatus and setTechnicalDebt with the appropriate values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A startRewrite function is defined that updates both legacyStatus and technicalDebt state values.
successCriteria: The startRewrite function is defined and calls setLegacyStatus('rewrite-in-progress') and setTechnicalDebt(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handler that initiates the rewrite process by updating the system status and resetting technical debt.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but it needs to update both state values: legacyStatus should become 'rewrite-in-progress' and technicalDebt should be reset to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The startRewrite function should be defined to update both state values. Try creating a function that calls setLegacyStatus and setTechnicalDebt.

steps.title: Create handler for making rewrite progress
steps.instruction: Create a function named makeProgress that increases the rewriteProgress state by 10 and updates the legacyStatus to 'modernized' when rewriteProgress reaches 100.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses setRewriteProgress to increment the current progress. Add a conditional check to see if the new progress is 100 or more, and if so, call setLegacyStatus to update the status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A makeProgress function is defined that increments rewriteProgress by 10 and updates legacyStatus when progress reaches 100.
successCriteria: The makeProgress function is defined, uses setRewriteProgress to increase progress by 10, and conditionally updates legacyStatus to 'modernized' when rewriteProgress reaches 100.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the makeProgress handler that simulates incremental progress on the rewrite project and updates the system status when complete.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but it may not fully implement the progress increment and status update logic. Make sure it increases rewriteProgress by 10 and updates legacyStatus when progress reaches 100.
steps.feedbackWrong: The makeProgress function is not correctly defined. Please create a function that increments rewriteProgress by 10 and updates legacyStatus to 'modernized' when progress reaches 100.

steps.title: Add structure and display current system status
steps.instruction: In your LegacyCodeSimulator component's return statement, add a container div with a heading that says 'Legacy System Dashboard' and display the current legacy system status, technical debt level, and rewrite progress in separate paragraphs.
steps.hint: Replace the current return null; with a div containing an h1 and three p elements that show the state values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a dashboard showing the current legacy system status, technical debt level, and rewrite progress.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing an h1 with 'Legacy System Dashboard' and three paragraphs displaying legacyStatus, technicalDebt, and rewriteProgress values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the UI structure to display the current system status, technical debt, and rewrite progress.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying all three state values (legacyStatus, technicalDebt, and rewriteProgress) in separate paragraphs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI structure isn't complete. Check that you're returning a div with a heading and paragraphs that display the current state values.

steps.title: Add control buttons and wire event handlers
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add three buttons: one labeled 'Add Technical Debt' that calls accumulateDebt when clicked, one labeled 'Start Rewrite' that calls startRewrite when clicked, and one labeled 'Make Progress' that calls makeProgress when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute to connect each button to its corresponding handler function. Place the buttons after the status display you added earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three interactive buttons appear below the status display, each wired to its corresponding handler function to simulate legacy system management decisions.
successCriteria: The component renders three buttons with labels 'Add Technical Debt', 'Start Rewrite', and 'Make Progress', each with onClick handlers calling accumulateDebt, startRewrite, and makeProgress respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the control buttons and wired them to their event handlers. This completes the interactive simulation for managing legacy code and rewrites.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check that all three required buttons are present with correct labels and onClick handlers. Make sure each button calls the right function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly implemented. You need to add three separate button elements with the specified labels and onClick handlers inside the return statement.
